claim: China's Export Control Law took effect on 1 December 2020.
evidence: "第四十九条　本法自2020年12月1日起施行。" (Art. 49; tr.: 'This Law takes effect on 1 December 2020.')

claim: Under Article 9 of the Export Control Law, China can impose temporary controls on items outside its control lists, for no more than two years, after which it must evaluate and cancel, extend or list them.
evidence: "可以对出口管制清单以外的货物、技术和服务实施临时管制……临时管制的实施期限不超过二年。" (Art. 9; tr.: 'may impose temporary control on goods, technologies and services outside the control lists... the period of temporary control shall not exceed two years.')

claim: Article 10 of the Export Control Law allows China, with State Council (and where relevant Central Military Commission) approval, to prohibit exports of controlled items outright or to specific countries, organisations or individuals.
evidence: "可以禁止相关管制物项的出口，或者禁止相关管制物项向特定目的国家和地区、特定组织和个人出口。" (Art. 10; tr.: 'may prohibit the export of relevant controlled items, or prohibit their export to specific destination countries and regions, specific organisations and individuals.')

claim: Article 12 of the Export Control Law creates a catch-all licence requirement for unlisted goods, technology and services where the exporter knows or should know, or is notified, that they may endanger national security and interests or be used for WMD or terrorism.
evidence: "出口经营者知道或者应当知道，或者得到国家出口管制管理部门通知，相关货物、技术和服务可能存在以下风险的，应当向国家出口管制管理部门申请许可：（一）危害国家安全和利益……" (Art. 12, para. 3)

claim: Article 18 of the Export Control Law establishes a control list of importers and end users (e.g. those violating end-use requirements or that may endanger national security), with whom exporters may not trade without special approval.
evidence: "国家出口管制管理部门对有下列情形之一的进口商和最终用户，建立管控名单……出口经营者不得违反规定与列入管控名单的进口商、最终用户进行交易。" (Art. 18)

claim: The Export Control Law punishes unlicensed exports with confiscation and fines of 5-10 times illegal turnover above RMB 500,000, or RMB 500,000-5 million where turnover is below that threshold.
evidence: "违法经营额五十万元以上的，并处违法经营额五倍以上十倍以下罚款；没有违法经营额或者违法经营额不足五十万元的，并处五十万元以上五百万元以下罚款" (Art. 34)

metric.name: Minimum fine for unlicensed export where illegal turnover is under RMB 500,000 (maximum RMB 5 million)

claim: Article 44 of the Export Control Law extends legal liability to organisations and individuals outside China that violate its export control provisions and endanger China's national security and interests.
evidence: "中华人民共和国境外的组织和个人，违反本法有关出口管制管理规定，危害中华人民共和国国家安全和利益……依法处理并追究其法律责任。" (Art. 44)

claim: Article 45 of the Export Control Law applies the law to transit, transshipment and re-export of controlled items.
evidence: "管制物项的过境、转运、通运、再出口……依照本法的有关规定执行。" (Art. 45)

claim: Article 48 of the Export Control Law authorises reciprocal measures against any country or region that abuses export control measures to endanger China's national security and interests.
evidence: "任何国家或者地区滥用出口管制措施危害中华人民共和国国家安全和利益的，中华人民共和国可以根据实际情况对该国家或者地区对等采取措施。" (Art. 48)

claim: China's Regulations on Export Control of Dual-Use Items (State Council Decree No. 792) were promulgated on 30 September 2024 and took effect on 1 December 2024, replacing four earlier dual-use regulations.
evidence: "《中华人民共和国两用物项出口管制条例》已经2024年9月18日国务院第41次常务会议通过，现予公布，自2024年12月1日起施行。" and Art. 50 repeals the nuclear, missile, biological and chemical dual-use regulations.

claim: Decree No. 792 provides three licence routes for dual-use exports: single licences valid up to 1 year, general licences valid up to 3 years, and export vouchers obtained by registration.
evidence: "单项许可的有效期不超过1年……通用许可的有效期不超过3年……以登记填报信息方式获得出口凭证" (Art. 15)

claim: Under Decree No. 792, MOFCOM must decide a dual-use licence application within 45 working days, but items with major national-security impact go to the State Council and are not bound by that deadline, and time for expert review or on-site checks is excluded.
evidence: "在45个工作日内作出准予或者不予许可的决定……不受前款规定出口许可审查期限的限制……所需时间不计算在本条第一款规定的出口许可审查期限内。" (Art. 17)

metric.name: Statutory review period for dual-use licence
metric.population: dual-use export licence applications (excluding those escalated to State Council)

claim: Decree No. 792 lets MOFCOM place importers and end users on a control list and prohibit, restrict or suspend dual-use transactions with them; exporters need approval to trade with listed parties.
evidence: "（一）禁止有关两用物项交易；（二）限制有关两用物项交易；（三）责令中止有关两用物项出口……特殊情况下确需进行有关交易的，出口经营者应当向国务院商务主管部门提出申请" (Art. 29)

claim: Article 49 of Decree No. 792 lets MOFCOM require foreign parties outside China to follow the regulations when transferring to specific destinations foreign-made items that contain, integrate or are mixed with specified Chinese-origin dual-use items, or are made with specified Chinese-origin technology.
evidence: "境外组织和个人在中华人民共和国境外……转移、提供下列货物……（一）含有、集成或者混有原产于中华人民共和国的特定两用物项在境外制造的两用物项；（二）使用原产于中华人民共和国的特定技术等两用物项在境外制造的两用物项" (Art. 49)

claim: Decree No. 792 itself sets no numeric value threshold for its extraterritorial rule; the 0.1% value threshold appears in MOFCOM Announcement 2025 No. 61, not in the Decree.
evidence: Reading of Decree 792 Art. 49 (no percentage) compared with Announcement 2025 No. 61 para. 1(1) ('价值比例达到0.1%及以上').
notes: Based on claim "Article 49 of Decree No. 792 lets MOFCOM require foreign par…" and claim "MOFCOM Announcement 2025 No. 61 (9 October 2025) would requi…". The unit question asked about a '0.1% value rule' in the regulations; it is in the announcement.

claim: China's unified Dual-Use Items Export Control List took effect on 1 December 2024 (Announcement 2024 No. 51), and 11 earlier notices were repealed that day, including the 2023 gallium/germanium notice (2023 No. 23), the 2023 graphite notice (2023 No. 39) and the 2024 antimony notice (2024 No. 33).
evidence: "现公布《中华人民共和国两用物项出口管制清单》（见附件1），自2024年12月1日起实施。同日，……等11个公告（见附件2）废止"; Attachment 2 lists "七、商务部、海关总署公告2023年第23号……八、……2023年第39号……十一、……2024年第33号".
notes: The Ga/Ge/graphite/Sb controls continue via the unified list; the original notices were repealed, not the controls.

claim: MOFCOM/GACC Announcement 2023 No. 23 made eight gallium items (metal, GaN, Ga2O3, GaP, GaAs, InGaAs, GaSe, GaSb) and six germanium items (metal, zone-refined ingots, ZnGeP2, germanium epitaxial substrates, GeO2, GeCl4) subject to export licensing.
evidence: "一、满足以下特性的物项，未经许可，不得出口：（一）镓相关物项。1.金属镓……2.氮化镓……3.氧化镓……4.磷化镓……5.砷化镓……6.铟镓砷……7.硒化镓……8.锑化镓……（二）锗相关物项。1.金属锗……6.四氯化锗"

claim: The gallium and germanium export controls under Announcement 2023 No. 23 were issued on 3 July 2023 and took effect on 1 August 2023.
evidence: "【发文日期】2023年07月03日" ... "八、本公告自2023年8月1日起正式实施。"
notes: Corroborates existing CLM-0344 with the tier-1 original.

claim: MOFCOM said the gallium and germanium controls do not target any specific country, that export control does not prohibit exports, and that it gave prior notice through the China-US and China-EU export control dialogues.
evidence: "It should be noted that export control does not prohibit exports, and exports that meet the relevant regulations will be allowed... China's measure does not target any specific country, and prior notifications had been provided through channels such as the China-U.S. and China-EU export control dialogues" (Shu Jueting, 6 July 2023)

claim: By late 2023 MOFCOM said it had approved some gallium and germanium export applications but gave no numbers.
evidence: "We have approved after review some of the export applications, and some companies have obtained export licenses for dual-use items. MOFCOM will continue to review the applications"

claim: MOFCOM/GACC Announcement 2023 No. 39 (20 October 2023) required export licences from 1 December 2023 for high-purity (>99.9%), high-strength, high-density synthetic graphite and for natural flake graphite and its products (including spherical and expanded graphite), while lifting temporary controls on other graphite items.
evidence: "（一）高纯度（纯度>99.9%)、高强度（抗折强度>30Mpa）、高密度（密度>1.73克/立方厘米）的人造石墨材料及其制品……（二）天然鳞片石墨及其制品（包含球化石墨、膨胀石墨等）" ... "九、本公告自2023年12月1日起正式实施"

claim: China's antimony and superhard-material export controls (MOFCOM/GACC Announcement 2024 No. 33) were announced on 15 August 2024 and took effect on 15 September 2024.
evidence: "2024年8月15日，商务部、海关总署联合发布公告，决定对部分锑、超硬材料相关物项实施出口管制，自2024年9月15日起正式实施。"

claim: MOFCOM's own explainer lists semiconductor components among antimony's uses and says superhard materials are indispensable for electronic-information industries.
evidence: "锑现已被广泛用于各种阻燃剂、合金、陶瓷、玻璃、颜料、半导体元件、电池技术……" (tr.: antimony is widely used in ... semiconductor components ...)

claim: MOFCOM Announcement 2024 No. 46 (3 December 2024) banned dual-use exports to US military users or uses and stated that gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard-material dual-use exports to the US would in principle not be licensed, with stricter end-user review for graphite.
evidence: "一、禁止两用物项对美国军事用户或军事用途出口。二、原则上不予许可镓、锗、锑、超硬材料相关两用物项对美国出口；对石墨两用物项对美国出口，实施更严格的最终用户和最终用途审查。"
notes: Tier-1 original for existing CLM-0346 (which cited a CSET translation).

claim: Announcement 2024 No. 46 states that organisations and individuals in any country who transfer the covered Chinese-origin dual-use items to US organisations or individuals will be held legally liable.
evidence: "任何国家和地区的组织和个人，违反上述规定，将原产于中华人民共和国的相关两用物项转移或提供给美国的组织和个人，将依法追究法律责任。"

claim: MOFCOM Announcement 2025 No. 72 (9 November 2025) suspended paragraph 2 of Announcement 2024 No. 46 (the US-specific gallium/germanium/antimony/superhard ban and graphite review) until 27 November 2026; paragraph 1 (ban on US military users) was not suspended.
evidence: "经批准，自即日起至2026年11月27日，商务部公告2024年第46号……第二款暂停实施。"
notes: Tier-1 confirmation of existing CLM-0347 (Xinhua). Only para. 2 is named; para. 1 remains.

claim: MOFCOM/GACC Announcement 2025 No. 10 (4 February 2025, effective on issuance) added export controls on tungsten, tellurium, bismuth, molybdenum and indium items, including indium phosphide, trimethylindium and triethylindium.
evidence: "五、铟相关物项（一）3C004.a．磷化铟……（二）3C004.b．三甲基铟……（三）3C004.c．三乙基铟" ... "本公告自发布之日起正式实施。"

claim: MOFCOM/GACC Announcement 2025 No. 18 (4 April 2025, effective on issuance) put export controls on seven medium and heavy rare earths: samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium and yttrium, including metals, alloys, targets, oxides and compounds.
evidence: Sections I-VII cover "Samarium related items ... Gadolinium ... Terbium ... Dysprosium ... Lutetium ... Scandium ... Yttrium related items"; "This announcement shall come into effect on the date of issuance."

claim: The April 2025 rare-earth controls cover sputtering targets (e.g. samarium, terbium and dysprosium targets) listed under reference customs code 8486909110, a code for parts of semiconductor-manufacturing machinery.
evidence: "Terbium-containing targets (Reference customs codes: 3824999922, 8486909110): a. Terbium target; b. Terbium-cobalt alloy target"
notes: HS 8486 = machines for manufacturing semiconductor devices; the 'parts' reading of 8486909110 is researcher knowledge, not stated in the source.

claim: MOFCOM Announcement 2025 No. 61 (9 October 2025) would require foreign exporters to obtain a Chinese dual-use export licence before exporting foreign-made listed items containing Chinese-origin listed rare-earth items worth 0.1% or more of the item's value, with this part due to take effect on 1 December 2025.
evidence: "含有、集成或者混有原产于中国的本公告附件1第一部分所列物项……且……价值比例达到0.1%及以上的" ... "本公告'一（一）'和'一（二）'部分自2025年12月1日起实施。"
notes: Tier-1 original for existing CLM-0348.

claim: Announcement 2025 No. 61 would also require licences for foreign-made listed items produced using Chinese-origin rare-earth mining, separation, metallurgy, magnet-making or recycling technology.
evidence: "（二）使用原产于中国的稀土开采、冶炼分离、金属冶炼、磁材制造、稀土二次资源回收利用相关技术在境外生产的本公告附件1所列物项"

claim: Under Announcement 2025 No. 61, applications whose end use is R&D or production of logic chips at 14 nm and below or memory chips of 256 layers and above, or equipment, test equipment and materials for making such chips, are reviewed case by case.
evidence: "四、最终用途为研发、生产14纳米及以下逻辑芯片或者256层及以上存储芯片，以及制造上述制程半导体的生产设备、测试设备和材料，或者研发具有潜在军事用途的人工智能的出口申请，逐案审批。"

claim: Announcement 2025 No. 61 states that applications for export to foreign military users, or to entities on China's export-control control and watch lists (including their 50%-or-more-owned subsidiaries), will in principle be denied.
evidence: "二、对向境外军事用户的出口申请，以及向出口管制管控名单和关注名单所列的进口商和最终用户（包括其控股50%及以上的子公司、分公司等分支机构）的出口申请，原则上不予许可。"

claim: MOFCOM Announcement 2025 No. 62 (9 October 2025, effective on issuance) controlled exports of rare-earth mining, separation, smelting, magnet-making and recycling technologies, and barred Chinese citizens and entities from giving substantive unlicensed support to such activities abroad.
evidence: "（一）稀土开采、冶炼分离、金属冶炼、磁材制造、稀土二次资源回收利用相关技术及其载体……七、中国公民、法人、非法人组织未经许可不得为境外稀土开采……活动提供任何实质性帮助和支持"

claim: MOFCOM/GACC Announcement 2025 No. 55 (9 October 2025) would have controlled superhard materials from 8 November 2025, including synthetic diamond micropowder, diamond wire saws and grinding wheels meeting set specifications, and DC arc plasma CVD equipment and process technology.
evidence: "三、2C902.c．具有以下所有特性的人造金刚石线锯……四、2C902.d．……人造金刚石砂轮……五、2B005.b．直流电弧等离子体喷射化学气相沉积（DCPCVD）设备" ... "本公告自2025年11月8日起正式实施。"

claim: MOFCOM/GACC Announcement 2025 No. 57 (9 October 2025) would have added export controls on holmium, erbium, thulium, europium and ytterbium items from 8 November 2025.
evidence: "一、1C909 钬相关物项……二、1C910 铒相关物项……三、1C911 铥相关物项……四、1C912 铕相关物项……五、1C913 镱相关物项" ... "本公告自2025年11月8日起正式实施。"

claim: MOFCOM/GACC Announcement 2025 No. 70 (7 November 2025) suspended Announcements 2025 Nos. 55, 56, 57, 58, 61 and 62 from that day until 10 November 2026.
evidence: "经批准，自即日起至2026年11月10日，商务部、海关总署公告2025年第55号、56号、57号、58号，及商务部公告2025年第61号、62号暂停实施。"
notes: Tier-1 confirmation of existing CLM-0349 (CIRS).

claim: The November 2025 suspension (Announcement 2025 No. 70) does not list the April 2025 rare-earth controls (Announcement 2025 No. 18), so those controls appear to remain in force.
evidence: Announcement 2025 No. 70 lists only Nos. 55-58, 61, 62; No. 18 is not named.
notes: From claim "MOFCOM/GACC Announcement 2025 No. 70 (7 November 2025) suspe…" and claim "MOFCOM/GACC Announcement 2025 No. 18 (4 April 2025, effectiv…". The White House May 2026 fact sheet's reference to yttrium and scandium shortages fits this reading.

claim: The White House said in November 2025 that China would issue general licences for exports of rare earths, gallium, germanium, antimony and graphite for the benefit of US end users, calling this the de facto removal of controls imposed since 2023.
evidence: "China will issue general licenses valid for exports of rare earths, gallium, germanium, antimony, and graphite for the benefit of U.S. end users and their suppliers around the world. The general license means the de facto removal of controls China imposed since 2023."
notes: US government's account of a bilateral commitment; no Chinese general-licence notice was found.

claim: The White House said in November 2025 that China would end its investigations targeting US companies in the semiconductor supply chain, including antitrust, anti-monopoly and anti-dumping investigations.
evidence: "China will terminate its various investigations targeting U.S. companies in the semiconductor supply chain, including its antitrust, anti-monopoly, and anti-dumping  investigations."

claim: The White House said China would suspend or remove non-tariff countermeasures taken since 4 March 2025, including listing US companies on its end-user and unreliable entity lists.
evidence: "China will suspend or remove all of the retaliatory non-tariff countermeasures taken against the United States since March 4, 2025, including China's listing of certain American companies on its end user and unreliable entity lists."

claim: In May 2026 the White House said China would address US concerns about shortages of rare earths and critical minerals including yttrium, scandium, neodymium and indium, and about restrictions on selling rare-earth production equipment and technology.
evidence: "China will address U.S. concerns regarding supply chain shortages related to rare earths and other critical minerals, including yttrium, scandium, neodymium, and indium. China will also address U.S. concerns regarding prohibitions or restrictions on the sale of rare earth production and processing equipment and technologies."

claim: As of 25 September 2026 the White House said the US and China were still working on US concerns about rare-earth and critical-mineral shortages, aiming to return shipments to appropriate levels.
evidence: "The United States and China continue to work on U.S. concerns regarding supply chain shortages related to rare earths and other critical minerals, with the goal of ensuring shipment levels return to appropriate levels."

claim: Asked in December 2025 how many rare-earth export licences had been approved since late October, MOFCOM gave no number and said all compliant civilian applications had been promptly approved.
evidence: "I would like to reiterate that all compliant export applications for civilian purposes have been promptly approved by the Chinese government." (MOFCOM press conference, 4 Dec 2025)

claim: China's Unreliable Entity List rules (MOFCOM Order 2020 No. 4) took effect on 19 September 2020 and target foreign entities that endanger China's sovereignty, security or development interests, or break normal market principles by cutting off normal transactions with Chinese firms or taking discriminatory measures against them.
evidence: "（2020年9月19日商务部令第4号公布 自2020年9月19日起施行）" ... "违反正常的市场交易原则，中断与中国企业、其他组织或者个人的正常交易，或者对中国企业……采取歧视性措施" (Art. 2)

claim: Listed entities on the Unreliable Entity List can be restricted or banned from China-related import/export and from investing in China, have staff entry and work permits restricted, and be fined.
evidence: "（一）限制或者禁止其从事与中国有关的进出口活动；（二）限制或者禁止其在中国境内投资；（三）限制或者禁止其相关人员、交通运输工具等入境；（四）限制或者取消其相关人员在中国境内工作许可……（五）根据情节轻重给予相应数额的罚款" (Art. 10)

claim: Chinese firms that need to trade with an entity banned under the Unreliable Entity List must apply to the working mechanism office for approval.
evidence: "中国企业、其他组织或者个人在特殊情况下确需与该外国实体进行交易的，应当向工作机制办公室提出申请，经同意可以与该外国实体进行相应的交易。" (Art. 12)

claim: On 9 October 2025 China's Unreliable Entity List working mechanism listed TechInsights Inc. and nine affiliates (including Strategy Analytics entities), together with 13 US defence-related entities, banning them from China-related import/export and new investment in China, and banning Chinese parties from transacting with them or sending them data.
evidence: "决定将反无人机技术公司、TechInsights公司及其分支机构等外国实体列入不可靠实体清单……一、禁止上述实体从事与中国有关的进出口活动；二、禁止上述实体在中国境内新增投资；三、禁止中国境内的组织、个人与上述实体进行有关交易、合作等活动，特别是向上述实体传输数据、提供敏感信息。"

claim: Whether the 9 October 2025 Unreliable Entity List listing of TechInsights was suspended under the November 2025 US-China arrangement could not be established from MOFCOM sources.
evidence: Searched: MOFCOM 5 Nov 2025 UEL spokesperson statement (covers only the 4 Mar and 4 Apr 2025 notices: 〔2025〕5, 6, 7号), MOFCOM 2025/2026 announcement lists; no notice on 〔2025〕10号 found.

claim: MOFCOM said that from 10 November 2025 China stopped the Unreliable Entity List measures of 4 March 2025 (notices 2025 Nos. 5 and 6) and suspended for another year the measures of 4 April 2025 (notice 2025 No. 7), to implement the Kuala Lumpur consensus.
evidence: "中方决定自2025年11月10日起，继续暂停4月4日公告（不可靠实体清单工作机制公告〔2025〕7号）相关措施1年，停止3月4日公告（不可靠实体清单工作机制公告〔2025〕5号和6号）相关措施。"

claim: MOFCOM said that from 10 November 2025 China stopped export-control-list measures against the 15 US entities of Announcement 2025 No. 13 and suspended for another year those against the 16 US entities of Announcement 2025 No. 21; exports to them now require a licence application.
evidence: "中方决定自2025年11月10日起，对第13号公告的15家美国实体停止上述相关措施；对第21号公告的16家美国实体继续暂停上述相关措施1年。出口经营者如需向上述实体出口两用物项，应当……向商务部提出申请"

claim: On 22 June 2026 MOFCOM put 10 US entities on its export-control control list, including rare-earth producers MP Materials Corp. and USA Rare Earth, Inc., banning dual-use exports to them and banning any party anywhere from transferring Chinese-origin dual-use items to them.
evidence: "一、禁止出口经营者对上述10家实体出口两用物项，禁止任何国家和地区的组织和个人将原产于中国的两用物项转移或提供给上述实体"; list items "9. 芒廷帕斯材料公司（MP Materials Corp.）" and "10. 美国稀土公司（USA Rare Earth, Inc.）".

claim: On 24 July 2026 MOFCOM put 14 EU entities on its export-control control list, including III-V Lab (France) and Vigo Photonics (Poland), both compound-semiconductor/photonics organisations.
evidence: "决定将拉法特集团等14家欧盟实体列入出口管制管控名单" ... "7.三五实验室（III-V LAB）" ... "9.维戈尔光电公司（Vigo Photonics S.A.）"
notes: Describing III-V Lab and Vigo as compound-semiconductor/photonics organisations is researcher knowledge, not stated in the notice.

claim: Since 2026 MOFCOM control-list notices (e.g. 2026 Nos. 23, 27 and 30) ban not only Chinese exporters but also foreign organisations and individuals from transferring Chinese-origin dual-use items to listed entities; the March 2025 notice (2025 No. 13) banned only exports to them.

claim: Under the Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law (10 June 2021), State Council departments can put individuals and organisations involved in foreign discriminatory measures on a countermeasure list and freeze their assets in China, deny visas, or ban transactions with them.
evidence: "第四条 国务院有关部门可以决定将直接或者间接参与制定、决定、实施本法第三条规定的歧视性限制措施的个人、组织列入反制清单。" Art. 6: "（二）查封、扣押、冻结在我国境内的动产、不动产和其他各类财产；（三）禁止或者限制我国境内的组织、个人与其进行有关交易、合作等活动"

claim: Article 12 of the Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law bars any organisation or individual from implementing or helping implement foreign discriminatory measures against Chinese citizens or organisations, and lets affected Chinese parties sue for an injunction and damages.
